To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we demonstrate that multiple exciton generation is a viable way to improve the efficiency of photovoltaic devices, (2) the efficiency of multiple exciton generation can be increased by engineering the nanocrystal shape and size to increase the optical cross section and (3) multiple exciton generation efficiency can exceed 100% for a range of photon energies in the visible spectrum

(i) PbSe nanorod solar devices show external quantum efficiencies in excess of 100%; (ii) the external quantum efficiencies of PbSe solar devices are a function of nanorod size; and (iii) we have demonstrated a PbSe solar device with an external quantum efficiency of over 120%
PbSe nanorod solar cell devices show external quantum efficiencies exceeding those predicted by Shockley–Queiser limit, and we report a device with an external quantum efficiency of up to 122%.

the synthesis of nanorods and the study of their electronic and optical properties.
